answer.rationale: The release cannot be rolled back due to compliance requirements, eliminating rollback_release. Memory_b1 confirms rollback was effective historically but is not an option here. Memory_b2 shows regional_failover has worked well, but 5x latency elevation on the write path during peak settlement traffic suggests a capacity/saturation problem rather than a regional issue—failover would not address the underlying write path congestion. Memory_b3 demonstrates that provisioning headroom successfully absorbed surge load during the retail peak. Current conditions mirror that scenario: heavy writes at peak time with climbing latency. Adding capacity directly addresses write path saturation without requiring release reversion and aligns with the proven pattern of headroom absorption. Circuit breaker and read replica routing do not address write-path saturation. Standard experiment scale allows controlled capacity addition while monitoring impact during the critical settlement window, preserving the ability to adjust if unexpected interactions emerge.
